global-vendetta.label: Global Standard — Vendetta
global-vendetta.notes: ARC/other printings are usable only when the same card name has a legal-set printing; preview-only future sets are excluded. ban_list_ref names the list in force; stale_on_or_after tracks the pool, which Radiance expands on 2026-10-23.

taiwan-set1-banned.label: Taiwan — Set 1 pool with global bans
taiwan-set1-banned.notes: Regional physical pool is OGN + OGS and does not move until Taiwan gets later-set product. The ban list layered on top is the global Constructed list and DOES move, which is why this entry names ban_list_ref rather than inheriting silently: when the global list is superseded this environment has changed, even though its card pool has not. Its stale_on_or_after stays null because that field tracks pool staleness; ban-list staleness is the gate's ban_list_ref check. A claim about coverage binds to the service snapshot, never to this live entry.

global-vendetta-2026-10-22.label: Global Standard - Vendetta, calibration snapshot
global-vendetta-2026-10-22.notes: The environment P4 calibrates against: the last day of the Vendetta pool before Radiance (2026-10-23). It is not stale after that date and never becomes stale - it is the historical record the official matchup data for this pool describes. status is scheduled_freeze, not frozen: global-vendetta is still live, and a ban-list change before 2026-10-22 would still move this content. On the freeze date the status becomes frozen and content_hash is filled with the digest of legal_set_ids plus the ban list in force; after that the entry is immutable and a change to it is a gate failure, not an update. On the freeze date it must also pin errata_overlay_version, errata_overlay_hash, effective_card_text_bundle_hash and ruleset_core_version, for the same reason the Taiwan service snapshot does; freeze_requires names them and the gate enforces it.

taiwan-set1-banlist-2026-07-24.label: Taiwan - Set 1 pool, ban list 2026-07-24, service snapshot
taiwan-set1-banlist-2026-07-24.notes: The environment P1's completeness claim binds to. Frozen now, not scheduled: both axes are already fixed - the Set 1 pool by physical distribution and the ban list by the 2026-07-24 version this entry names. A later global ban list does not change this snapshot; it produces a new one, and P1's claim then states which snapshot it covered. legal_for_play is false because play legality is always the live entry plus a live re-check, never a frozen record. Codex 2026-09-09: a completeness claim also depends on effective card text and the rules baseline, so the snapshot pins the errata overlay version and hash, the digest of every legal card's errata-resolved text, and the Core Rules version. A later erratum or Core Rules update changes one of those hashes and the claim is then visibly about a different snapshot, rather than silently false.
